title: How Agent Memory Works
summary: Follow one small fact from Koko's chat into a later conversation—and see every gate in between.

truthLadder.analogy: Agent memory is a tiny backpack of labeled cards, not a recording of every moment.
truthLadder.mechanism: A memory system selects candidate facts, stores approved records with context, retrieves relevant matches, and places a few into a future prompt.
truthLadder.caveat: Implementations differ. A recalled record may be stale, irrelevant, or wrong, so it should be checked and remain correctable.

overview.title: One fact's whole journey
overview.caption: The salmon fact moves through five distinct stages; click any stage to jump to Koko's question.

nodes.label: Chat context
nodes.detail: The fact exists for this run

scenes.title: The temporary whiteboard
scenes.question: Michi, why won't an agent remember every chat forever?
scenes.simpleAnswer: A chat is like a whiteboard: useful now, but temporary unless something is saved.
scenes.technicalAnswer: The active context carries current messages for this run. Durable memory is a separate write, not an automatic property of the conversation.
scenes.caveat: Some products retain chat history, but history and actively retrieved agent memory are not the same thing.
scenes.takeaway: Current context and durable memory are different stores.

visuals.caption: The fact reaches temporary context, then disappears from active use unless another step writes it.

visuals.title: Temporary context versus durable memory
visuals.caption: These stores serve different jobs even when both contain the same words.

nodes.label: Chat history
nodes.detail: A record is not automatically recalled

scenes.title: The memory gate
scenes.question: Then what decides whether my salmon fact gets saved?
scenes.simpleAnswer: A gate checks whether the fact is useful, safe, and allowed to keep.
scenes.technicalAnswer: A write policy can test relevance, sensitivity, user intent, duplication, and retention rules before persistence.
scenes.caveat: A responsible gate rejects secrets and low-value noise; exact rules vary by system.

visuals.title: The write decision
visuals.caption: A candidate reaches durable storage only after the policy approves it.

visuals.title: Many messages, very few memories
visuals.caption: A selection funnel narrows chat content without pretending every message deserves persistence.

scenes.title: A labeled record
scenes.question: Where does a safe memory sleep?
scenes.simpleAnswer: It sleeps on a labeled card with the fact, its source, and when it was learned.
scenes.technicalAnswer: The system persists a structured record and indexes useful fields or an embedding so later retrieval can find it.
scenes.caveat: A store may be a file, database, vector index, or combination; the card is only an analogy.
scenes.takeaway: Useful provenance travels with the remembered fact.

visuals.title: What a useful record carries
visuals.caption: The remembered fact stays more trustworthy when source and time travel with it.

nodes.label: Search index
nodes.detail: Find it by meaning or fields

visuals.title: Who talks to whom during a write
visuals.caption: The write crosses a policy boundary before the index and durable store accept it.

visuals.title: The memory's lifetime
visuals.caption: A durable record still changes meaning over time and must be checked when recalled.

scenes.title: Finding the right card
scenes.question: How does a new agent find that fact later?
scenes.simpleAnswer: It searches for cards related to the new question and brings back only the best matches.
scenes.technicalAnswer: A retriever converts the new request into search criteria, ranks candidate records, and injects a limited relevant subset into the active context.
scenes.caveat: Retrieval can miss a useful record or return a misleading one, especially when wording or context changes.
scenes.takeaway: Recall is a search step, not magic awareness.

visuals.title: Search, rank, and select
visuals.caption: The new question connects to several records, but only the strongest useful match enters context.

visuals.title: Why the salmon fact wins
visuals.caption: Illustrative bars make ranking visible without claiming these are measurements from a real product.
visuals.chartNote: Teaching-only relevance scores; actual retrieval models and score scales differ.

scenes.title: Memory is a clue
scenes.question: Does a recalled memory become automatically true?
scenes.simpleAnswer: No. Michi treats memory as a useful clue and checks whether it still fits.
scenes.technicalAnswer: The agent should evaluate relevance, freshness, provenance, and conflicts before relying on a retrieved record, while allowing correction or deletion.
scenes.caveat: A fluent answer can still misuse a correct record, so retrieval quality alone does not guarantee answer quality.

visuals.title: Check before use
visuals.caption: Confidence sends the answer down one branch; uncertainty sends a question back to Koko.

visuals.title: Memory stays correctable
visuals.caption: A later answer can produce feedback that updates or removes the old record before the next retrieval.

teachBack.question: What turns a temporary chat detail into durable memory?
options: An approved write after the memory gate
The chat simply being long enough
teachBack.explanation: Durability requires a separate write. Length and confidence do not create persistent memory.

teachBack.question: Why does retrieval rank candidate memories?
options: To bring only the most relevant records into limited context
To permanently delete every weak match
To prove that every stored fact is current
teachBack.explanation: Ranking selects useful context for this request; it neither deletes weak matches nor proves freshness.

teachBack.question: What should happen when a recalled record may be stale?
options: Check it or ask the user before relying on it
Treat it as true because it was stored
Hide it and invent a replacement
teachBack.explanation: Memory is evidence to evaluate, not automatic truth. Uncertainty should be visible and correctable.
